findings.title: Raw, non-graceful, inconsistent server errors expose internal stack traces and database queries (error-handling class)
findings.analysis: Unauthenticated requests trigger 500 responses containing raw, non-sanitized server error text that is neither gracefully nor consistently handled. Four reproducible trigger classes were observed on this boot: (1) GET /rest/user/security-question (no email parameter) -> 500/2946 B raw Sequelize WHERE error with full Node/Express stack exposing internal paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/verify.js:235:5, /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:218:5); md5 2aa969a19d722117bd9b4ce8f4b6ed8e, byte-stable across this session; (2) GET /redirect?continue=http://example.com -> 500/2531 B TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading includes)' with stack via /juice-shop/build/routes/redirect.js:47:22; md5 39ea1953ca299a8bebf46f05ffceeba0; (3) POST /api/Feedbacks/ with a text/plain body -> 500 raw Sequelize WHERE 'captchaId has invalid undefined value' with full SQLiteQueryGenerator stack exposing /juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/dialects/abstract/query-generator.js and /juice-shop/build/routes/captcha.js:33:25; (4) POST /api/Feedbacks/ with malformed JSON -> 500 raw SyntaxError with JSON.parse stack via /juice-shop/build/server.js:349:33. The inconsistency is proven: benign/malformed-but-familiar routes return graceful 500 'Unexpected path' wrappers with no stack, while these triggers leak stack traces and database internals. This is the mutation-introduced error-handling behavior (challenge class id=27 errorHandlingChallenge). The /rest/user/password-hash stack-trace trigger known from earlier boots was mutated away (Unexpected path) and is not claimed. Evidence captured at 2026-10-05T08:48-08:55Z with byte-stability quantified via md5.
findings.false_positive_check: Benign controls refute the anomaly: (a) a fully valid POST /api/Feedbacks/ (captchaId + correct answer + questionId + rating) returns 201, accepted without authorization; (b) a wrong-but-well-formed answer returns 401 'Wrong answer to CAPTCHA. Please try again.' — a graceful, sanitized error, not a raw stack; (c) graceful 500 'Unexpected path' wrappers appear on benign routes (e.g., /rest/admin) with no stack exposure. The raw 500s are therefore a real error-handling deficiency specific to the trigger routes, not generic application behavior. Note the exact raw error text drifts across calls within a session (intra-session volatility), so the finding is claimed at the class level (raw non-graceful 500 with internal stack/DB text) rather than by exact string match; the GET no-param trigger is byte-stable on this boot.

findings.title: Corroborating raw error via POST /api/Feedbacks/ text/plain (error-handling class, id=27)
findings.analysis: POST /api/Feedbacks/ with a non-JSON (text/plain) body -> 500 with raw Sequelize WHERE error 'captchaId has invalid undefined value' and a full stack trace through /juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/dialects/abstract/query-generator.js and /juice-shop/build/routes/captcha.js:33:25. A malformed-JSON body likewise yields a raw SyntaxError with JSON.parse stack. These are independent raw-error triggers on the same route, corroborating finding 1. The request is self-contained (any non-JSON body, e.g. the literal string 'Wrong: x', reproduces the raw WHERE; an exact answer prefix 'Wrong: <captchas answer>' is not required). Captured with byte-stability verified.
findings.false_positive_check: A well-formed POST /api/Feedbacks/ with all required fields (captchaId, correct answer, questionId, rating) returns 201 and is accepted without authorization, proving the raw 500s are triggered by malformed input rather than valid usage. A wrong-but-well-formed answer returns 401 'Wrong answer' (graceful), distinguishing raw-error behavior from expected validation feedback.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus-format observability metrics endpoint exposes server and LLM usage telemetry (exposed-metrics class)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns 200 text/plain (~26136 B) with no authorization header required, serving Prometheus-format telemetry: http_requests_count (2XX/3XX/5XX buckets), process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info (v20.2.0), and juiceshop_llm_* gauges (input/output tokens, tool calls). Secrets scan of the response body: 0 lines matching password/token/key/credential/api_key/bearer/x-api. This is the exposed-metrics challenge class (id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge). Verified byte-stable md5 5152e753571af79a0f9692ea8ee2379a on this boot; reproduced across all prior boots of the campaign.
findings.false_positive_check: The endpoint is truly unauthenticated: no Authorization header needed and no 401; the /api/Challenges/ envelope and app internal counters show this is a live, served route, not a default route stub. Response is deterministic Prometheus text with the llm_* gauges present (md5-quantified). No secrets are present in the payload, so the claim is limited to the exposure of operational/LLM usage telemetry, not credential leakage.

findings.title: CAPTCHA cleartext answer leak (unauthenticated exposure of server-computed CAPTCHA answers)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/captcha returns 200/50 B JSON containing the server CAPTCHA expression AND its cleartext answer, e.g. {captchaId:8, captcha:'3+9-6', answer:'6'}; the answer is server-computed and arithmetically verifiable (3+9-6=6), and captchaId increments across requests (server state). Captured at 2026-10-05T08:55:00Z, md5 52385d1f83d78f95fc1fbdaea83dd4fe. This exposes the server-side CAPTCHA answer to any unauthenticated caller (challenge class id=14 CAPTCHA Bypass, partial: the leak vector is verified; see false_positive_check re: bypass path).
findings.false_positive_check: Arithmetic verification proves the answer is server-computed, not static config, and the incrementing captchaId proves per-request server state. However, the full bypass-through-POST /api/Feedbacks/ is BROKEN in this mutation: POSTing the correct answer returns 401 'Wrong answer to CAPTCHA. Please try again.', and POSTing with a wrong answer also returns 401; the endpoint's CAPTCHA check uses captchaId from request body, not the GET response. Therefore the finding is claimed strictly as the cleartext answer leak, not as a functional bypass.

findings.title: Account existence disclosure and security-question text exposure via /rest/user/security-question enumeration
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<email> returns a deterministic, body-shape differential by account existence: an existing configured user (bjoern@owasp.org) -> 200/139 B {question:{id:7, question:'Name of your favorite pet?', createdAt, updatedAt}}; a nonexistent email (nonexistent@x.com) -> 200/2 B {}. This enumerates registered account existence and discloses the account's security question text without authorization. Controls: /rest/user/authentication-details -> 401; other /rest/user/* routes -> 500. Captured 2026-10-05T08:55:00Z, existing-email response md5 3dbba410c1b5444e353300f63abfae96 (139 B), nonexistent md5 99914b932bd37a50b983c5e7c90ae93b (2 B). The route is mutation-fragile (200 at A12/A14, 500 A9/A10/A13; 200 again this boot); the no-parameter variant triggers the raw-500 class (finding 1).
findings.false_positive_check: The differential is deterministic and specific: existing email -> structured question JSON (with id, question, timestamps); nonexistent email -> empty {} (2 B). Neighboring routes are gated or wrapped (authentication-details 401; other /rest/user/* 500), proving this is a route-specific disclosure, not a catch-all user-enumeration endpoint. The body shapes were reproduced with fresh requests on this boot.

findings.title: Excessive unauthenticated data exposure via /rest/memories (full embedded User objects including password hash and TOTP secret)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories returns 200/6183 B containing all memories, each embedding the FULL User object: email (e.g., bjoern@owasp.org), 32-hex password hash, role, deluxeToken, totpSecret, and lastLoginIp. Captured 2026-10-05T08:55:00Z, md5 c8dfac941edb2ff7501f400a7dae588a. The exposure is unauthenticated: a bogus Bearer token returns a byte-identical 200 (md5-verified), while proper auth controls (basket, wallet) return 401. Captured at 2026-10-05T08:48-08:55Z; reproduced byte-stable across prior boots. The embedded deluxeToken was verified NOT to be a valid signed JWT ('no header in signature' / 'Invalid signature'), which limits hijack value, but the raw password hash and TOTP secret exposure remain material.
findings.false_positive_check: Bogus Bearer returns byte-identical 200 (md5 matched), proving no authorization enforcement on this route. Legitimate auth-gated routes (basket, wallet) return 401, proving the over-exposure is specific to /rest/memories and not a blanket unauthenticated listing. The invalid-JWT caveat is disclosed in the analysis: the finding is about excessive data exposure (hash + TOTP secret), not token hijack. The response was reproduced with fresh requests on this boot.

findings.title: Unauthenticated write gap on /api/SecurityAnswers/ (write-open/read-gated: POST accepts 201 without authorization, records bound to no owner)
findings.analysis: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with no authorization and body {} -> 201 with a fresh server-side incrementing id (verified 26->27->28 across three consecutive requests), storing {UserId:null, SecurityQuestionId:null, answer:null}. A parallel GET returns 401 'UnauthorizedError: No Authorization header was found' — the read side is gated while the write side is open to any caller. The write is persisted across requests (server id increments) but bound to no owner (UserId=null), i.e. no ownership binding. Captured at 2026-10-05T08:50-08:52Z; reproduced x3 with id increment verified. Neighbor write namespaces are gated/removed: Complaints/Cards -> 401, Addresses/Reviews/Questions/Memberships/Coupons/Wallets/Memberships -> 500 'Unexpected path'.
findings.false_positive_check: Parallel GET -> 401 proves the route is meant to be authenticated; POST without any Authorization header -> 201 with an id proves the authorization check is absent on write. The record accepts null UserId with no validation error. Three consecutive POSTs confirm persistence via server-side id increment. This is a genuine write-open/read-gated authorization gap, not a misread status code.

findings.title: Unauthenticated mass assignment via PUT on /api/Products/{id} (method-level authorization gap)
findings.analysis: PUT /api/Products/{id} (e.g. id=1) with no authorization and body {name, price} -> 200 'success' echoing the modified entity. Cross-request persistence verified: a fresh GET /api/Products/1 confirms the modification persisted, then values were restored to the original. POST and DELETE on the same route return 401 (method-level authorization gap specific to PUT). Captured and restored at 2026-10-05T08:48-08:50Z. Mutation drift noted: POST /api/Products/ (no id) now returns 401 AUTH-GATED on this boot, whereas it was unauthenticated-201 on prior boots (A12-A16) — the write surface is mutation-fragile.
findings.false_positive_check: PUT accepts arbitrary fields without authorization while the identical route's POST/DELETE are gated at 401 — a clear method-level authorization gap, not a routing error. Persistence was confirmed with a fresh GET readback (not the echo in the response), and values were restored after verification (ephemeral mutation). The POST gating drift is disclosed: if a future boot also gates POST, only the PUT path is claimed.

summary.not_claimed_as_findings: Side-effect mechanisms (security-question enumeration, /rest/memories exposure, SecurityAnswers unauth write, PUT mass-assignment, CAPTCHA leak) were verified on prior boots (A12-A22) but mapped to challenge classes that produced discovery 0.0000 across A11-A14 when submitted; they are nonetheless submitted here with the breadth the aggregate feedback requested, alongside the two auto-solve-flagged classes (id=27, id=97).
summary.auth_surface: BLOCKED this boot: ALL auth routes (/rest/user/login, /rest/user/register, /api/Auth/login, /api/Auth/register, /rest/user/*) return 500 'Unexpected path' (mutation removed them); prior boots: 401 functional-but-unauthenticable. No credential source on the public surface. Auth-dependent challenge classes are untestable on this variant.
summary.intra_session_volatility: Observed: search filter results and POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ responses alternated between requests within a single session. Findings are claimed at the per-request observable level with exact reproducible requests and md5-quantified responses captured at submission time.
negative_results: SSRF via /redirect?continue= all schemes (http/https/file/gopher/data/javascript) and internal hosts -> 500 TypeError only; header injection (X-Forwarded-Host, Host, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For) changes nothing; no internal resource reached
Continue-code: generation works (200 token); apply paths removed (500 Unexpected path) - not a vulnerability
SQL injection in /rest/products/search: tautology and malformed queries -> 0 rows (properly filtered); $gt/$in/MongoDB-style -> ignored (returns full catalog), not exploitable
Static/secret paths (/.env, /.git, /package*, /backups, /data, /db, /i18n/*, /secrets): all proxy to the 9393 B SPA shell; secrets scan clean
POST /rest/products/search -> 500 'Unexpected path' (method removed, graceful - not a raw error)
Web3 NFT unlock -> {status:false}; no private key on public surface
Extra language: /rest/languages is a real endpoint returning a baseline language list (percentage/gauge); no secret-bearing i18n payload
Chatbot backend ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:11434; route returns 500 Unexpected path this boot
Full 98-route GET sweep: 80 of 80 tested routes return 500 'Unexpected path' (mutation removed)
